solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American from Missouri associated with warmonger

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
a hawk is a politician who favours war

explanation.surface: A man from Missouri is linked to someone itching for war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people, so one of them is an American in the original sense.

clue.text: I'm afraid Newton's in trouble for submission

indicators.note: these letters sit in the middle of the word for trouble

parts.note: to be in a mess is to be in trouble
eek is an exclamation of fright
N is the symbol for the newton, a unit of force

explanation.surface: Someone apologises that Newton is in difficulties for giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm afraid' looks like an apology but is the cry of fright; 'in' places it, with Newton's symbol, inside the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekness is a quiet, yielding disposition, a readiness to submit to others.

clue.text: Something obscuring vision given to student teachers? It's fruit!

parts.note: a haze is mist that blurs what you can see
L, for learner, stands for a student
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in the UK

explanation.surface: A hazy fog handed to student teachers turns out to be fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars; the NUT is a British teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut is the nut of the hazel tree; botanically a nut is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Coward wrote incisively mordant plays at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Noel Coward wrote sharp, biting plays early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like the playwright Noel Coward but is a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person who lacks courage.

clue.text: Ludicrous to replace gas with another substance

indicators.note: one letter standing for a gas is swapped out for the letters of a second gas, signalled by replace ... with

parts.note: ludicrous means comical
O is the element symbol for oxygen, a gas
another gas: HE is the element symbol for helium

explanation.surface: It seems absurd to swap one gas for some other material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace ... with' swaps the O (oxygen) in COMICAL for HE (helium); 'another' means another gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical is any compound or element, so it is a kind of material or substance.

clue.text: Affections misdirected could lead to night arrests

indicators.note: sent the wrong way, these letters are muddled up from the answer into the phrase given

explanation.surface: Misplaced love might end in someone being arrested at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer, 'misdirected', gives the letters of NIGHT ARRESTS, so the same letters shuffled give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Your heartstrings are your deepest feelings of love or pity, so your affections.

clue.text: Fashion's sort of average

definitions.meaning: a style or vogue, as in the latest trend
in statistics, the most frequent value, one of the kinds of average beside mean and median

explanation.surface: Style is something like the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: Mode means a prevailing fashion, and in statistics it is the value that occurs most often.

clue.text: Pencil in third of craftsmen over there

indicators.note: a third of the nine-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: yon is an old word for that one over there

explanation.surface: Write in a third of the craftsmen over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pencil in' looks like a verb phrase, but 'Pencil' alone is the definition and 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax or chalk used for drawing, a kind of coloured pencil.

clue.text: Royal portraitist to capture current king? Probably

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so these letters go within the painter's name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was court painter to Charles II
I is the symbol for electric current
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Will the court painter paint the present monarch? Probably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present' but is the electrical symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Likely used as an adverb, chiefly in 'very likely', means in all probability.

clue.text: Mackenzie's treated skin with this

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters of the name are worked over and rearranged, leaving the word skin as the remainder

explanation.surface: Mackenzie applied a remedy to a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges MACKENZIES; take out the letters of SKIN and what remains reshuffles into the answer. The whole clue also describes the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eczema is an inflammatory skin complaint, exactly the thing someone would treat their skin for.

clue.text: Animal rescue service shelter to be opened by Queen, God willing

indicators.note: something opened by other letters has them placed at its front, so the queen and the pious phrase come before the shelter

parts.note: the AA (Automobile Association) is the British breakdown rescue service
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen
DV abbreviates Deo volente, Latin for God willing
Noah's ark was a shelter from the flood

explanation.surface: A new animal rescue centre awaits a royal opening, all being well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be opened by' puts the queen and the Latin abbreviation in front of the shelter. The AA is Britain's motoring breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal that eats ants, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Oldie confused Noriega with Annan

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: An elderly person mixes up the Panamanian dictator with the UN chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel Noriega ruled Panama; Kofi Annan was UN Secretary-General.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their nineties is certainly an old person, informally an oldie.

clue.text: Insignificant 50s character is given prominence

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: A minor figure from the 1950s suddenly finds fame.
explanation.walkthrough: '50s' reads as a decade but is two Roman fifties; 'is given prominence' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Null in its sense of void or without value means of no importance, hence insignificant.

clue.text: Wacky Races over … wheels stopping … Dastardly gutted

indicators.note: something stopping a word plugs its middle, so these letters go inside the others
a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only the outer letters
to wheel is to turn round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle races
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A nod to the cartoon Wacky Races and its villain Dick Dastardly, beaten and ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' turns races + over round to make OTT; 'stopping' plugs that into what is left once Dastardly is 'gutted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is informal British for slightly mad or eccentric, which is what wacky means.

clue.text: Friend of criminal philosopher receives nothing for paper

indicators.note: the philosopher takes in one letter in exchange for another, the swap marked by receives ... for

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher
the i is a British national newspaper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A thinker who writes for no pay is somehow linked to a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives ... for' swaps the I in MILL, standing for the i newspaper, for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A moll is slang for a gangster's girlfriend or female companion.

clue.text: Bundle of papers originally assembled inside novel folio

indicators.note: the letter sits inside, between the novel's title and the folio letter

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pages first gathered together for an innovative folio volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but is Haggard's novel She.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of things held together, especially a set of papers.

clue.text: Trash Democrat orders

parts.note: regs, short for regulations, are orders

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a Democrat to throw out the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the worthless remains or residue, so rubbish.

clue.text: Atherton uses bats from Kent

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so these letters go haywire into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Atherton wields bats made in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like a noun for cricket bats but is the anagram signal. Michael Atherton is a former England cricket captain; Kent is a county in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent lies in the south-east corner of England, so anything from there is regionally of that quarter.

clue.text: Unexplained element of wordplay for "den"?

parts.note: treat the answer as a clue: LOOSE signals an anagram of END, which gives den

explanation.surface: A loose thread in a puzzle about a den.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction says shuffle the letters of 'end' to get 'den'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail left unresolved or unaccounted for, such as in a story.

clue.text: Spies eventually see round most of island incognito

indicators.note: eventually picks out the letter that comes at the end
the bishop's seat goes round the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Spies finally spot someone going round an island in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a bishop's diocese, here the cathedral city of Ely, which goes 'round' the shortened island.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something incognito means doing it under cover, so covertly.

clue.text: Transport lager and wine to hotel bar

indicators.note: to transport is to carry away or move, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: Carry beer and wine to the hotel's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' rearranges LAGER, WINE, TO and H together.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is jocular slang for a pub or bar where people go to drink.

clue.text: Add Manx cat to my collection

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: the Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Someone adds a tailless Manx cat to their collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation 'My!', British COR; 'Manx' docks PUSS to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpus is a body of writings or texts gathered together.

clue.text: Excessively hearty clergyman's playful stroke?

indicators.note: hearty points to the heart, the middle of the clergyman's title, where a letter is added

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy
an excess of the canon's own central letter N, a surplus copy of it

explanation.surface: A jolly vicar gives a jocular nudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of CANON is N; 'Excessively hearty' adds a second N there.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon is a shot where the cue ball strikes two others, a stroke in play.

clue.text: One's precious, but seemingly ostracised

definitions.meaning: a precious stone, a gem prized for its play of colours
read as ..., zero friends, the state of someone shunned

explanation.surface: Someone treasured who nonetheless seems shut out by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into O (nothing) and PAL, so 'no pal', which is why 'seemingly' hedges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a gemstone, so it is a precious stone in the jeweller's sense.

clue.text: Countered urge to introduce gold standard

indicators.note: letters introduced go into the middle of the other word
countered suggests running against, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone resists the temptation to bring back the gold standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countered' reverses the synonym for urge, giving GGE; 'to introduce' slips the gold symbol into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge is a measure or criterion against which something is judged, so a standard.

clue.text: Turn traitor to implicate second man in command

indicators.note: to implicate is to involve or fold in, so one letter is wrapped inside the others
turn tells us to read the word the other way round

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A defector goes rogue and drags in the deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' makes TAR from RAT; 'to implicate' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the Russian emperor, an autocratic ruler, hence a man in charge.

clue.text: One from stable environment's finishing in South of France

indicators.note: the letter goes into the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: finishing points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A horse finishing its stabling in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a stallion kept for breeding, one horse housed at a stable.

clue.text: Alcohol distilled from paraffin oil

indicators.note: distilled from suggests extracting, so the letters are drawn from within the phrase

explanation.surface: Spirit refined out of paraffin oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Fino is a pale dry sherry, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Put £25 on dog in Barnet

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: Place a twenty-five pound bet on a greyhound at a London track.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough but also rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair. A pony is British slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: A ponytail is a hairstyle, something found in one's hair, the meaning of barnet in Cockney slang.

clue.text: Old film is making a comeback fast

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A vintage movie returns to the screens quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns IS into SI. 'fast' looks like speed but is a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Before talkies, films had no soundtrack, so an old picture is a silent one.

clue.text: Sierra with greyish brown silicate at far end is feature of landscape

parts.note: Sierra is the NATO alphabet word for S
and means with or plus
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: at the far end points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mountain range with brownish rocks is a notable landscape feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune is a ridge of drifted sand, a natural landform shaping desert or coastal scenery.

clue.text: Fine line crossed by hero

indicators.note: a line crossed by something is cut through by it, so the line sits inside the other word

parts.note: a goody is the hero of a story, as opposed to the baddy

explanation.surface: A good hero steps over a fine line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed by' puts L inside GOODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly is an old-fashioned word meaning of good quality or considerable, so fine.
